what_its_for: Calcifediol is a form of Vitamin D used to treat secondary hyperparathyroidism (overactive parathyroid glands) in adults who have stage 3 or 4 chronic kidney disease (CKD) and low levels of Vitamin D in their blood. Your kidneys are not able to properly activate regular Vitamin D, so this special form helps make up for that.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or break open the capsule. Take it at bedtime. Try to take it at the same time each night to help you remember. Drink plenty of water unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 30 mcg (micrograms) taken by mouth once daily at bedtime. Your doctor may increase your dose to 60 mcg once daily at bedtime after about 3 months if your blood levels are still too low. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to find the right dose for you. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose at bedtime, take it as soon as you remember that same night. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular bedtime. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose. Doubling up can cause dangerously high calcium levels in your blood.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired capsules safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other Vitamin D supplements (including cod liver oil, multivitamins with Vitamin D, or over-the-counter Vitamin D pills) unless your doctor specifically approves them — taking too much Vitamin D can cause dangerous high calcium levels. Avoid antacids or other products that contain magnesium unless your doctor says it is okay. Limit foods very high in calcium or Vitamin D while on this medication unless directed by your doctor or dietitian. Tell your doctor before starting any new prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite that is unusual for you; feeling very tired or weak; feeling confused or having trouble thinking clearly; increased thirst or urinating much more than normal; muscle pain, bone pain, or muscle weakness; headache; irregular or fast heartbeat; constipation; or any new or worsening symptoms. These could be signs of too much calcium or Vitamin D in your blood, which can be serious.
when_it_works: Calcifediol starts working gradually. Your doctor will check your blood levels of Vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D), calcium, phosphorus, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) about every 3 months to see how the medication is working. It may take several weeks to months before your blood levels reach the right range. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Kidney Disease: This medication is specifically designed for people with stage 3 or 4 chronic kidney disease. Your doctor will closely monitor your kidney function and blood levels while you are on this medication. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. High Vitamin D levels can be harmful to an unborn baby or nursing infant. Elderly Patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to Vitamin D and calcium changes — your doctor will monitor you carefully. Children: This medication has not been studied in children and is approved for adults only.
